facts.raw_span: 4-week history of watery diarrhea (20 episodes per day)
vomiting
diffuse abdominal pain aggravated by spicy foods
8-kg weight loss (≈15% of body weight)
brownish macules on the hands and feet
hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk
onychodystrophy
mild hypoproteinemia and hypoalbuminemia (total protein 3.52 g/dL [normal 6.6–8.3], albumin 2.09 g/dL [3.5–5.2])
zinc deficiency (51 µg/dL [70–120])
low vitamin B12 (<150 pg/mL [300–900])
multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa
numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum

rationales.F01: Watery diarrhea is a common symptom in gastrointestinal disorders, but the high frequency and duration suggest a more severe condition.
rationales.F05: Brownish macules on the hands and feet are a characteristic feature of Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome.
rationales.F11: Multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa are highly suggestive of Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome or Familial Adenomatous Polyposis.
rationales.F12: Numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum are highly suggestive of Familial Adenomatous Polyposis or Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of brownish macules on the hands and feet, hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk, and onychodystrophy, along with multiple type II and III Yamada polyps on atrophic gastric mucosa, specifically supports Peutz-Jeghers Syndrome.
